geography noun

classical

Cic. Att. 2.4.3

Traupman 204, 320

geōgraphia, geōgraphiae f.

noun, first declension

Greek γεωγραφία, the description of the earth. Cicero promised Atticus a geography (Att. 2.4.3) and soon had second thoughts: magnum opus est (2.6.1). A map is tabula geōgraphica (see map).

Examples

  • dē geōgraphiā dabō operam ut tibi satis faciam; sed nihil certī polliceor. magnum opus est

    On the geography, I’ll do my best to satisfy you; but I promise nothing definite. It’s a big jobCic. Att. 2.4.3

  • dē geōgraphiā etiam atque etiam dēlīberābimus

    about the geography, I shall think it over again and againCic. Att. 2.7.1

See also map, world, globe, history, subject.
